answer:
**Review: streaming-ingest (Clickstream ingestion, eu-central-1)**

Finding 1 [high · Reliability · REL10-BP01] OpenSearch runs in 1 Availability Zone with no dedicated master nodes, against a 99.9% availability target. The best practice asks for managed data services to be deployed with multi-AZ replication and failover. [S12][S14]

Finding 2 [high · Reliability · REL05-BP04] The SQS dead-letter queue has manual redrive, no age alarm and 4-day retention, so failed events can expire unnoticed. The best practice calls for DLQ alarms, message-age measurement and a planned redrive or clearing of backlog. [S4]

Finding 3 [medium · Reliability · REL10-BP01] Aurora has one writer and zero reader replicas. Aurora replicates data across AZs by default, but no failover target is configured to meet the 60-minute RTO. [S12]

Finding 4 [medium · Reliability · REL09-BP01] Aurora backup retention is 1 day. The best practice asks that all data be backed up, with recovery time fitting within the RTO and RPO. Point-in-time recovery is available for supported data stores. [S15]

Finding 5 [low · Operational Excellence · OPS08-BP04] The settings show no alarms for the Kinesis stream or the Lambda consumer, only none for the DLQ. The best practice asks for actionable alerts tied to KPIs, with composite alarms to reduce alert fatigue. [S5]

- **Security:** no gap found in the settings. Kinesis and Aurora use KMS encryption at rest. The settings do not show encryption in transit for producers and consumers, which the Data Analytics Lens asks for [S6]. Please confirm this.
- **Performance Efficiency:** no gap confirmed. The Kinesis shard quota for eu-central-1 is 6,000, so 4 shards are within quota [get_service_quota]. I could not retrieve per-shard write capacity, so I cannot confirm whether 4 shards cover the expected peak of 6 MB/s. Please check this figure. Shard planning guidance is in [S20].
